-- CC_0177_mo_legislature_incumbents.sql
-- St. Louis MO deep seed, wave 2 (occupancy half). Slot RESERVED from the allocator.
-- Applied back to back with CC_0176, which creates the 2 chambers and the 197 offices.
-- GENERATED by backend/data/seed-st-louis-mo-2026/occupancy-scripts/gen_cc0177.py from
-- mo-occupancy-2026-09-28.json. Edit the generator, not this file.
--
-- Seats 188 of the 197 members of the 103rd Missouri General Assembly -- 155 representatives and
-- 33 senators -- and flags the other 9 seats vacant. Creates 187 people and REUSES 1.
--
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 🔴🔴 EVERY term_start HERE IS AN OCCUPANCY START, NOT A TERM START. Ruled 2026-09-28 (Cantrell).
-- essentials.office_terms models OCCUPANCY -- seat_officeholder closes the predecessor the day
-- before, and re-election does not end an occupancy -- so a Missouri representative re-elected in
-- 2024 did not begin a new occupancy on 2025-01-08.
--
--   123 terms  2023-01-04  the member is certified at THIS district number in the 102nd General
--                          Assembly's first-day Journal and has held it continuously since
--    65 terms  2025-01-08  the member is first certified at this district in the 103rd
--
-- ⚠ THIS DELIBERATELY DIFFERS FROM CC_0157 (Kansas) AND CC_0164 (South Dakota), which wrote the
-- CURRENT TERM START -- 119 of 125 Kansas House members carry 2025-01-13 regardless of how long
-- they had served. That is the documented fallback and it is cheaper. Missouri's Journals sell the
-- deeper answer for the cost of two PDFs per chamber, so the fallback was not needed here.
--
-- 🔴 THE FLOOR IS AT 2023-01-04 BECAUSE THAT IS WHERE THE GEOGRAPHY STOPS BEING TRUE. Production
-- holds only 2022-plan polygons. House District 78 before January 2023 covered different ground,
-- so reaching occupancy back to 2021 or 2019 would make essentials.office_holders_as_of() name the
-- right person for territory that district did not cover. The 100th (2019) and 101st (2021)
-- Journals were downloaded and read, and are deliberately NOT used.
--
-- 🟢 THE EVIDENCE IS KEYED BY DISTRICT NUMBER, SO NO NAME MATCHING IS REQUIRED ANYWHERE. Each
-- first-day Journal prints the Secretary of State's s 115.525 RSMo certification as a numbered
-- list -- "78th Rasheen Aldridge Jr." -- on the day the oath was administered. That is what makes
-- the homonym traps below harmless: nothing here is resolved by a name.
--   The House Journal itself disambiguates Brown 149 / Brown 16 / Brown 27 / Brown 87,
--   Smith 46 / Smith 155 / Smith 163, Taylor 48 / Taylor 84, Johnson 12 / Johnson 23 -- and lists
--   ⚠ Sharp 37 and Sharpe 4, two different people one letter apart.
--
-- ⚠ NEITHER ROSTER FIELD CAN BE TURNED INTO A DATE, AND BOTH WERE TESTED. The House publishes
-- 'Elected:' (an election year) and 'Years Served:' (years in the CHAMBER, not in the district).
-- Mark Matthiesen (HD-107) reads 'Elected 2016' with 6 years served, and John Simmons (HD-109)
-- reads 'Elected 2024' with 6 -- both are gaps in service that no arithmetic recovers. The
-- Journals date both exactly: Matthiesen is certified at HD-107 in the 102nd, so he carries
-- 2023-01-04; Simmons held HD-109 in 2019 and 2021, LOST IT TO KYLE MARQUART IN 2023, and returned
-- in 2025, so his current occupancy starts 2025-01-08.
--
-- 🔴 HD-2 IS A SURNAME CHANGE, NOT A CHANGE OF PERSON. The 102nd Journal certifies 'Mazzie Boyd'
-- and the 103rd certifies 'Mazzie Christensen'; the roster's independent 'Elected' field reads
-- 2022 for both. Matching on the name alone writes 2025-01-08 and understates her occupancy by two
-- years. Resolved from house.mo.gov/MemberDetails.aspx?district=002&year=2023, which names
-- Christensen at the 2023 seat.
--   🟢 That page got its own control, because a departed official's URL can serve their successor:
--   ?district=109&year=2023 returns Kyle Marquart and &year=2025 returns John Simmons, so the year
--   parameter is honoured and the read is real. HD-2 was the ONLY contradiction in 197 seats.
--
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 🔴🔴 SIX NAMES ALREADY EXIST IN PRODUCTION. FIVE ARE DIFFERENT PEOPLE AND ONE IS THE SAME
-- PERSON. Getting either direction wrong is silent.
--
--   Mike Jones         (HD-12) -- production's Mike Jones holds PENNSYLVANIA State House 93
--   Michael Johnson    (HD-23) -- production's Michael Johnson holds SOUTH CAROLINA Senate 16
--   Chad Perkins       (HD-40) -- production's Chad Perkins holds MAINE State House 31
--   David Tyson Smith  (HD-46) -- production's David Smith holds FLORIDA State House 38
--   Brian Williams     (SD-14) -- production's Brian H Williams is an INDIANA Superior Court judge
--
-- Each of those five currently holds a seat in another state, and nobody holds two at once, so
-- none can be the Missourian; new people are created with the duplicate-name guard lifted for that
-- one statement.
--
-- 🔴🔴 A full_name SWEEP IS NOT THE GUARD'S TEST, AND MISSED TWO OF THE FIVE.
-- essentials.politician_name_duplicate_guard() keys on
--   lower(btrim(first_name)) AND lower(btrim(last_name)), over ACTIVE rows only.
-- 'David Tyson Smith' and 'David Smith' have different full names and the SAME (first, last), and
-- so do 'Brian Williams' and 'Brian H Williams'. The full_name sweep found 4 of 6; the guard threw
-- on the 5th during the dry run. occupancy-scripts/gen_guardcheck.py now applies the guard's own
-- predicate to all 188 -- run it before regenerating this file.
--
-- 🟢 THE REUSE SET WAS SWEPT THREE WAYS, and the third sweep found a real match, so it was not
-- blind: an exact-name join (4 hits, above); a last-name + first-initial sweep restricted to rows
-- carrying stances or a Missouri race (35 hits, every one an officeholder in another state, 0 with
-- a Missouri race); and a sweep of the 105 JOURNAL name forms, which returned Denny Hoskins --
-- SD-21's senator in the 102nd, now MISSOURI SECRETARY OF STATE and already seated in production
-- with 14 stances. He is a PREDECESSOR, never a holder here, so no action -- but he is the
-- positive control that proves the sweep can find something.
--
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 🔴 NINE SEATS ARE VACANT: House 29, 95, 99, 110, 114, 149, 159, 160 and Senate 10. They get
-- offices.is_vacant and NO term row. Per CLAUDE.md a vacancy span whose start date is unknown must
-- NOT be written, and no resignation letter or writ of special election has been read for any of
-- them. essentials.vacate_office() is deliberately NOT used: it requires a first vacant day.
--   SD-10's vacancy has the Senate's own notice -- senate.mo.gov/senators/ carries
--   Senators/VacantSenator?district=10 and the text "Vacant District 10" -- not merely an absent
--   member card. The eight House vacancies carry the member grid's literal 'District Vacant', and
--   are confirmed a second way: those 8 detail pages are exactly the 8 publishing no 'Elected'
--   value.
--
-- 🔴 is_incumbent IS SET EXPLICITLY ON EVERY INSERT. It defaults to false since CA_0188, and a
-- seated person inserted without it is HIDDEN from address search.
--
-- 🔴 PARTY IS NOT WRITTEN. The House grid carries it (105 R, 50 D); party lives on
-- races.primary_party, never on a person.
--
-- 🟢 THE RESERVED external_id BAND IS -2790388 .. -2790202 (187 ids), MEASURED EMPTY on 2026-09-28
-- with margin either side, against a control on South Dakota's band that correctly returned 105.
--
-- ⚠ A GENERAL ELECTION FALLS FIVE WEEKS AFTER THIS WAS MEASURED (2026-11-03) and the 104th General
-- Assembly convenes in January 2027. Everyone seated here is correct TODAY. SD-4 is already known
-- to change: Karla May is term-limited and Gina Mitten won the August primary. Current occupancy
-- is seeded; the winners of an election that has not happened are not.
--
-- Idempotent: every INSERT is NOT EXISTS-guarded and both UPDATEs are guarded. Ends with a
-- post-verify gate.
